provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — inbound emails with links to newly-registered typosquat/brand-spoof domains are detectable at the mail gateway/proxy via URL reputation and lookalike-domain analytics, but the social lure content itself is hunt-leaning.

high — execution of a fake installer/macro document spawning CrashReporter.exe or a rundll32-launched PE from user-download/temp paths, immediately after opening a lure document, is a strong process-lineage detection via EDR (process creation, parent-child, Office-spawns-child).

high — PowerShell script-block/module logging captures downloader cradles, TCP reverse-shell socket code, and Unicorn-style downgrade/injection patterns; suspicious PowerShell launched from Office/installer lineage adds context.

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: high — cmd.exe spawned by an anomalous parent (a Windows service host / SUGARUSH process) with an outbound TCP socket is a strong EDR process-creation + network-correlation detection.
high — rundll32.exe launched by a child of an Office/Excel process, or loading a non-standard DLL/PE from a user path, is a high-fidelity EDR detection (rundll32 abuse + Office-spawns-child).

detection_candidates.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
detection_candidates.rationale: high — new service creation (Event ID 7045 / service-install) named 'Service1' pointing at an unusual binary is directly observable and actor-specific; pair with the outbound port-4585 connection for high confidence.

high — service-launched execution of an untrusted binary is observable via service-install and process-creation telemetry (parent = services.exe), especially correlated with the 'Service1' name and reverse-shell network activity.

high — scheduled-task creation (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational) with the misspelled 'CrashRepoeter...TaskMachineUA' name and a CrashReporter.exe action in TabRoaming is an actor-specific, high-fidelity detection.

detection_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — legitimate-looking names in unusual paths (CrashReporter.exe in TabRoaming, DebugLogWindowsDefender.txt in %TEMP%) are detectable via name/path/hash baselining and signature-vs-name mismatch, but require tuned rules.

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
detection_candidates.rationale: high — a non-browser process opening browser 'Login Data'/profile SQLite files and User Data directories across multiple browsers is a strong EDR file-access/credential-theft detection.
high — a non-browser process reading browser cookie stores across Chrome/Edge/Opera/Firefox profiles is detectable via EDR file-access telemetry, alongside the same process's credential-store access.

medium — outbound download requests to actor staging IPs/domains followed by new-executable file writes are detectable via proxy/DNS + process/file telemetry, but generic downloader traffic needs the IOC context to stand out.
high — outbound TCP to the fixed non-standard port 4585 (especially to the known SUGARUSH C2) originating from a service-host/backdoor process is a crisp network + host-correlated detection.

medium — HTTP C2 to the specific actor IPs is detectable via proxy/netflow when those indicators are watchlisted, but generic HTTP beaconing blends with normal web traffic without the IOCs or beacon-cadence analytics.

medium — the NorthStar C2 stager and its C2 beacon are detectable via known-payload hashes and outbound connections to the C2 IP, but the framework itself is generic and requires the actor IOCs/behavioral signatures.

medium — Base64-encoded blobs in outbound SMTP/HTTP bodies are detectable via DLP/content inspection and the 'CrashLog.txt'/'VLC Player' artifacts, but encoding alone is common and needs pairing with the exfil-channel context.

medium — the encryption is implemented in-malware over plain HTTP, so the encrypted payload is detectable as high-entropy content to the actor C2 IP, but the crypto itself provides no standalone network signature without the IOC/host context.

high — an endpoint process making direct outbound SMTP (port 587) connections to smtp.yandex.com / smtp.mail.yahoo.com and sending a 'CrashLog.txt' attachment (subject 'VLC Player') to the john.macperson mailboxes is a strong host+network detection, since direct client-to-webmail SMTP from a workstation is anomalous.

high — creation of %TEMP%\DebugLogWindowsDefender.txt by the stealer followed by an HTTP POST of encrypted data to 144.202.123.248 is detectable via correlated file-write + process + netflow telemetry against the watchlisted C2 IP.

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — high-entropy/encoded staging files (DebugLogWindowsDefender.txt, CrashLog.txt) in %TEMP%/user paths are detectable via file-entropy and name-pattern analytics, but require dedicated scanning to surface.

medium — tunneled C2 is detectable via anomalous long-lived outbound sessions and known-tunnel process/port signatures, but generic tunneling blends with normal encrypted traffic without corroborating indicators.

medium — use of legitimate webmail as a relay blends with normal traffic; detectable when direct workstation-to-webmail SMTP is baselined as anomalous and correlated with the stealer process, but not from the destination domain alone (which is legitimate).

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — malware development is an off-victim adversary activity; intel/attribution candidate. Downstream execution of the developed malware is where host detection lands.
low — tool acquisition is off-endpoint; intel/hunt candidate. The downstream use of each tool (Metasploit stagers, NorthStar C2 beacons) is the detectable surface.
low — adversary domain registration is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via typosquat/brand monitoring and newly-registered-domain tracking.
low — actor-controlled webmail accounts are off-victim; intel candidate. On-victim, outbound SMTP to these specific mailboxes is the detectable behavior (see SUGARDUMP exfil TTP).

low — staging of a watering hole and fake-login infrastructure occurs off-victim / on third-party sites; intel/hunt candidate via web content-integrity monitoring of your own login pages and phishing-infrastructure tracking.

low — the watering-hole compromise is on a third-party legitimate site and the initial visitor beacon blends with normal web traffic; hunt candidate via egress to the watering-hole C2 and web-content-integrity monitoring of partner/owned login pages.
low — user clicks on links are largely a human/social action; hunt candidate correlating proxy/DNS resolution of actor typosquat domains with the user that browsed them.

low — credential capture happens on actor-controlled fake portals, off-victim; hunt/intel candidate via detection of employees resolving/browsing the fake-login typosquat domains and post-compromise anomalous logins to the spoofed services.
low — OS/version enumeration is common and largely benign; meaningful only within the malware's process-lineage context, so a hunt rather than a standalone detection.
low — abuse of a trusted third-party site is outside the victim's own telemetry; hunt/intel candidate via monitoring partner/supplier web assets and egress to the watering-hole C2.
